lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: contingency and accessibility planning

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic contingency and accessibility planning task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner revisits a route plan, either their own from earlier in the unit or a new one, develops a specific contingency plan for at least one realistic failure point, then revises that plan to account for one accessibility need.
safetyNotes: This task is planning only; the learner does not need to travel the route or experience an actual disruption as part of the lesson.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific way thinking about the accessibility need changed how you'll plan any transportation route in the future, not just this one.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Contingency plan specificity: Learner names a specific, realistic failure point and a specific backup plan with a clear step-by-step explanation. | Accessibility reasoning: Learner names a specific accessibility need and explains a specific, logical change to the route or backup plan because of it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner plan a contingency for a second, different type of failure (such as a weather event instead of a missed connection) and compare how the backup plan differs between the two situations.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic contingency and accessibility planning task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: contingency and accessibility planning worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner revisits a route plan, either their own from earlier in the unit or a new one, develops a specific contingency plan for at least one realistic failure point, then revises that plan to account for one accessibility need.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact contingency and accessibility planning decision or action.
Model move 2: Think of a time a trip didn't go as planned, yours or someone else's.
Model move 3: Pick a route plan and identify one realistic way it could fail.

Model check: Contingency plan specificity: Learner names a specific, realistic failure point and a specific backup plan with a clear step-by-step explanation. | Accessibility reasoning: Learner names a specific accessibility need and explains a specific, logical change to the route or backup plan because of it.

resources.title: contingency and accessibility planning action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for contingency and accessibility planning.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: contingency and accessibility planning coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner revisits a route plan, either their own from earlier in the unit or a new one, develops a specific contingency plan for at least one realistic failure point, then revises that plan to account for one accessibility need.
Coach direction: Think of a time a trip didn't go as planned, yours or someone else's.
Learner prompt: Describe what went wrong and what happened next.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: contingency and accessibility planning complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Pick a route plan and identify one realistic way it could fail.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I identified a specific failure point in my route (such as a missed connection, a closed route, or a significant delay).
Response 2 (t2-p2): I wrote a specific backup plan for that failure point (an alternate route, a later departure, or a different mode).
Response 3 (t2-p3): Explain step by step what you would do if the failure happened, from noticing the problem to arriving at your destination.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: contingency and accessibility planning minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one specific way thinking about the accessibility need changed how you'll plan any transportation route in the future, not just this one.

Success checks: Contingency plan specificity: Learner names a specific, realistic failure point and a specific backup plan with a clear step-by-step explanation. | Accessibility reasoning: Learner names a specific accessibility need and explains a specific, logical change to the route or backup plan because of it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: contingency and accessibility planning supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional contingency and accessibility planning condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Contingency plan specificity: Learner names a specific, realistic failure point and a specific backup plan with a clear step-by-step explanation. | Accessibility reasoning: Learner names a specific accessibility need and explains a specific, logical change to the route or backup plan because of it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner revisits a route plan, either their own from earlier in the unit or a new one, develops a specific contingency plan for at least one realistic failure point, then revises that plan to account for one accessibility need.

simulationRoute.title: contingency and accessibility planning — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the contingency and accessibility planning task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain one specific way thinking about the accessibility need changed how you'll plan any transportation route in the future, not just this one.
observableCriteria: Contingency plan specificity: Learner names a specific, realistic failure point and a specific backup plan with a clear step-by-step explanation.
Accessibility reasoning: Learner names a specific accessibility need and explains a specific, logical change to the route or backup plan because of it.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Contingency plan specificity: Learner names a specific, realistic failure point and a specific backup plan with a clear step-by-step explanation. | Accessibility reasoning: Learner names a specific accessibility need and explains a specific, logical change to the route or backup plan because of it.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
